The Router appropriately marked limb-related checkpoints as untestable due to occlusion/cropping. I agree with all verdicts; the Router was not too lenient.

The animal_pose_auditor reported a HIGH artifact risk (82% low-confidence keypoints), which strongly supports the Router's observation of structural ambiguity, particularly in the face and limbs. Although the pose auditor is trained on real animals, such widespread low confidence in a close-up usually indicates subtle anatomical warping or 'melting' that confuses the keypoint detector. The topology auditor found a clean mask, but this does not rule out internal structural softness. I agree with the Router's severity ratings but note that the high pose uncertainty suggests the artifacts are more pervasive than just the snout edge, affecting the overall structural definition.

The subject conforms well to the taxonomic description for a non-male sea lion.
artifact_reasoning: The image suffers from subtle AI-generation artifacts. The animal_pose_auditor's high low-confidence ratio (0.82) indicates significant structural ambiguity, likely due to slight melting or lack of sharp anatomical definition in the head and hidden limbs. The Router correctly noted 'painted' fur texture and soft boundaries at the snout. While not catastrophic, these issues prevent the image from achieving high structural integrity scores. The artifacts are noticeable upon close inspection (severity ~2-3 range).
